ch13.sub: Creator and Sovereign of Our Universe
ch13.sum: Michael of Nebadon is a Creator Son originating in the Universal Father and the Eternal Son, and to our universe and all its inhabited worlds he is, for all practical purposes, God. He was born a creator, yet he chose to earn his sovereignty through the experience of seven creature bestowals. The last of these was his life on Urantia as Jesus of Nazareth, a life that revealed the Father in the flesh and at the same time revealed man to God. This chapter considers the Creator Son as an only-begotten Son, the sovereignty he earned by experience, Christ Michael as God incarnate in man, and the ministry and eternal destiny of the Master Son. Michael's story is one in which power becomes authority through service, and the Creator comes to understand his creatures' hearts by living their life.
ch13.s1.u1.k: A Creator Son is the maker and ruler of a local universe, each one an only-begotten Son.
ch13.s1.u1.p: Creator Sons share the traits of Father and Son, yet they are not stamped from one mold. Each is the only-begotten offspring of the united original concepts of the two perfect Creator minds, the absolute of the deity concepts that constitute his origin. The ancient confession of an only-begotten Son is read anew in the Urantia Book as the uniqueness of each Creator Son.
ch13.s1.u2.k: The relationship of the Father and the Creator Son is touching, and it is the wellspring of all parental love.
ch13.s1.u2.p: Even amid the vast work of organizing a universe, a Creator Son always enjoys the sustaining approval of the Father. The text calls this relationship touching. The nearly divine love that human parents bear their children has its source in the deep affection of the Deity parents for their divine offspring. When we love our children, we reflect a love that first flowed in heaven.
ch13.s1.u3.k: To our universe Michael, the Creator Son, is to all practical intents and purposes God.
ch13.s1.u3.p: All of the Paradise Deity that mortals can discerningly comprehend is personified in Michael. He is a ruler and parent as mighty and beneficent as the Father and the Eternal Son would be if both were present ruling on Salvington. For us, then, Michael is the supreme personality. Before seeking God afar off, we meet God through him, the father of our universe.
ch13.s2.u1.k: Michael was born a creator, but he was required to earn his sovereignty by experience.
ch13.s2.u1.p: Creatorship alone would justify full sovereignty, yet the Michaels choose not to claim it but to earn it by experience. As freewill Sons they could have done otherwise. Michael too was born a creator yet had to earn his sovereignty by experience, and the arena of its final experience was our small world. Choosing experience over prerogative determined the character of his rule.
ch13.s2.u2.k: Bestowal experience makes a Creator a wise, sympathetic, and understanding sovereign.
ch13.s2.u2.p: Bestowal is inherent in the nature of the Paradise Sons; their desire to come close to the lives of their subordinate creatures reflects the nature of the Deities who gave them being. A Creator Son is innately just and merciful, but the experience of living as a creature leads him to an understanding mercy, merciful in new ways. A ruler's wisdom and sympathy deepen when he stands where the ruled stand.
ch13.s2.u3.k: Michael's death on Urantia completed his bestowal career.
ch13.s2.u3.p: The words "It is finished" spoken on the cross gain a literal meaning in the Urantia Book: it was the moment when a Creator Son who had completed six bestowals finished the seventh. Thereafter Michael ruled not as the Father's vicegerent but as sovereign in his own name, and when the Universe Mother Spirit subordinated herself to him, all power in heaven and on earth was committed to him.
ch13.s3.u1.k: The great mission of the final bestowal was to reveal God by a life devoted to doing the Father's will.
ch13.s3.u1.p: The purpose of the Urantia bestowal lay less in founding a new doctrine than in living a life. A life lived with wholehearted motivation to do the Father's will was itself the revelation of God in the flesh. That revelation was directed above all to the creatures of the flesh, to us. In the life of Jesus, God appears not as an object of doctrine but as the Father made visible in a human life.
ch13.s3.u2.k: Christ Michael was not God in association with man but God incarnate in man.
ch13.s3.u2.p: Debate over the divinity and humanity of Jesus has run through the whole history of Christianity. The text speaks plainly: he was of dual origin but not a double personality; he neither became God by degrees nor became man at some moment. He was always God and man. What grew was not his identity but his human mind's awareness of that fact.
ch13.s3.u3.k: Incarnational bestowal is the greatest of miracles, yet within it the Father worked in his usual way.
ch13.s3.u3.p: For citizens of the local universe miracles are few, and the most intriguing of them is that a divine Son should be born into a world by apparently natural processes. Yet even within that extraordinary experience the Father worked as he always does, in the normal, natural, and dependable way. God's greatest works are accomplished less through spectacular wonders than within ordinary life.
ch13.s4: The Ministry and Destiny of the Master Son
ch13.s4.u1.k: Michael's sovereignty unites the divine will with creature experience, and is supreme without being arbitrary.
ch13.s4.u1.p: In his personal sovereignty Michael combines the divine will of the universal Creators with the understanding experience of his local universe creatures. His power comes from experienced association with the Paradise Deities, and his authority from actual experience as a creature, so that his sovereignty holds both the view from above and the view from below. Authority born of understanding wins trust without compulsion.
ch13.s4.u2.k: The Master Son maintains unbroken communication with his bestowal worlds through the Spirit of Truth.
ch13.s4.u2.p: Having finished his bestowal, Michael is not one who has gone away. Through his spiritual presence, the Spirit of Truth poured out upon all flesh, he remains in touch with his bestowal worlds. His sympathetic reach extends from the Father on high to the lowly races in the realms of time. The presence of Christ is not only a memory in history but a reality experienced here and now.
ch13.s4.u3.k: Michael reveals the Supreme and is destined to be forever the way, the truth, and the life for all personalities.
ch13.s4.u3.p: Through seven bestowals Michael revealed the seven wills of the Trinity, and in their synthesis the will of the Supreme, thus identifying himself eternally with the Supreme Being. When Jesus said, "I am the way, the truth, and the life," it was more than the declaration of an age. In eternity the Michaels will be those who light the path ahead for all personalities.
ch13.qs1: What does Michael's choice to earn by experience the sovereignty he could have claimed by right teach me about how I hold authority?
ch13.qs2: How does understanding Jesus as God incarnate in man change the way I read his life?
ch13.qs3: If God's greatest works are done within ordinary life, what meaning does my ordinary day hold?
ch14.sub: Creative Spirit, Divine Minister, Holy Spirit
ch14.sum: When a Creator Son goes forth to build a local universe, the Infinite Spirit sends with him a unique representation of himself. This Creative Spirit is at first his associate in physical organization; at the time of life creation she becomes a personal Mother Spirit, the Divine Minister; and after Michael's final bestowal she is raised to be his coruler. Through the seven adjutant mind-spirits she fosters evolving mind, and as the Holy Spirit she awakens and guides the human soul. This chapter considers in turn her origin and growth, her partnership with the Son, her ministry to mind, and the leading of a Spirit who never drives. The universe is one family watched over by a fatherly Son and a motherly Spirit.
ch14.s1: The Creative Daughter of the Infinite Spirit
ch14.s1.u1.k: The Creative Spirit is a new and unique representation the Infinite Spirit individualizes to accompany a Creator Son.
ch14.s1.u1.p: A local universe is not the work of a lone creator. At the very moment a Creator Son is personalized, the Infinite Spirit prepares a companion to go with him. Because both respond to physical and spiritual realities alike, they become co-ordinate associates who complement each other in the government of the local universe. The pairing is planned from the beginning.
ch14.s1.u2.k: At the time of life creation the Creative Spirit becomes a personal Mother Spirit, the Divine Minister.
ch14.s1.u2.p: Through the long ages of physical organization the Creative Spirit was a less personal associate. But when Michael proclaims the creation of life and Paradise gives its approval, she appears as a distinct person in the presence of the Creator Son. That is why she is known in Satania as the Divine Minister. Because she has become a person, true partnership with the Son becomes possible.
ch14.s1.u3.k: The Mother Spirit's career keeps growing through the postbestowal ages and the ages of light and life.
ch14.s1.u3.p: The Mother Spirit does not remain a finished being from the start. Her career has stages, and each adds new status and experience. When the Son completes his bestowals and attains sovereignty she is lifted up as cosovereign, and in the age of light and life she enters a still greater experience that cannot yet be described. Even a divine being grows along with the universe.
ch14.s2: The Partnership of Son and Spirit
ch14.s2.u1.k: The Son and the Spirit preside over the universe as a father and mother watch over their children.
ch14.s2.u1.p: This picture of the local universe as a family carries more than metaphorical weight. Its creatures are the children of the Son and the Spirit together, and in no creative act does one proceed without the counsel and approval of the other. The numerous orders of spirit personalities, the angels among them, are wholly the Mother Spirit's responsibility. Universe order rests on the co-operation of parents.
ch14.s2.u2.k: After his bestowals Michael made the Mother Spirit coruler and proclaimed her equality.
ch14.s2.u2.p: When the Mother Spirit first pledges her loyalty to the Son, Michael answers by acknowledging publicly his eternal dependence upon her. In this scene a pledge of subordination is met by a proclamation of equality, and it shows the character of universe government. Authority appears as rank, but what flows within it is a love that honors the other. The dignity of universe government shows in the one of highest rank honoring his companion.
ch14.s2.u3.k: The Divine Minister helps the space-bound Son so that together they transcend time and space.
ch14.s2.u3.p: The Creator Son is not hindered by time but is limited by space; he cannot be in two places at once. The Mother Spirit, by contrast, is free of space but must reckon with time. When the two work as one, each one's limitation is made up by the other's freedom. A partnership that supplies what the other lacks is what enables them to care for an entire local universe.
ch14.s3.u1.k: The seven adjutant mind-spirits are the Mother Spirit's offspring, circuits through which her consciousness unfolds.
ch14.s3.u1.p: The seven adjutant mind-spirits accompany the Life Carriers to a new planet and become the ground on which the mind of primitive life grows. The seven adjutants, from intuition to wisdom, are less independent persons than circuits through which the Mother Spirit's consciousness unfolds on many levels, always subordinate to her action and presence. From animal instinct to human judgment, she is present wherever mind grows.
ch14.s3.u2.k: When the adjutants of worship and wisdom function, mind crosses the threshold of spiritual ministry.
ch14.s3.u2.p: The first mark that sets man apart from the animal is not tools or language but the impulse to worship. The spirit of worship is the badge that forever distinguishes the mind creature from soulless beings. When this impulse grows together with wisdom, the mind is at once drawn into the spiritual circuits of the Mother Spirit. The capacity to adore opens the door to spiritual life.
ch14.s3.u3.k: Mind is a bestowal of divinity, yet it is not immortal apart from spirit identification.
ch14.s3.u3.p: Mind ascends from the mechanical level through the adjutant level to supermind. Yet even the highest intellect does not survive of itself. The key to survival lies not in the size of intelligence but in spiritual insight, the capacity to worship and to crave survival. This is why the Mother Spirit's ministry ever draws mind toward spirit.
ch14.s4: The Leading of the Holy Spirit
ch14.s4.u1.k: The Holy Spirit is the Mother Spirit's spiritual circuit, forming with the Adjuster and the Spirit of Truth a symmetry of endowment in man.
ch14.s4.u1.p: What the scriptures call the Spirit of God sometimes means the Infinite Spirit and sometimes the Creative Spirit of the local universe. The Holy Spirit is the spiritual circuit of the latter and works within the local universe. Man receives together the Father's Adjuster, the Son's Spirit of Truth, and the Spirit's Holy Spirit. Gifts from three sources meet in one person and enable him to realize his sonship with God.
ch14.s4.u2.k: The Holy Spirit's ministry is partly independent of human attitude, yet grows more effective as man follows divine leading.
ch14.s4.u2.p: The Spirit of Truth works only as far as man receives it, but the Holy Spirit ministers in part regardless of human attitude. Yet even this ministry deepens when it meets the co-operation of the will. Sanctifying and spiritualizing the inner life is the joint work of a gift from above and a response from below. Grace comes first, but it grows within response.
ch14.s4.u3.k: The Spirit never drives; it meets us as we are and gently leads.
ch14.s4.u3.p: The divine Spirit does not wait on high but descends by long steps to meet man where he is. Then it embraces that soul and stays with it all the way on the journey back upward. Yet this leading always presupposes willing co-operation; a forced step is not the Spirit's way. A heart willing to learn is the condition for being led by the Spirit.
ch14.qs1: When I see the universe as a family cared for by a fatherly Son and a motherly Spirit, how does my relationship with God look different?
ch14.qs2: How do the urges toward worship and wisdom show themselves in my daily life, and how am I nurturing them?
ch14.qs3: If the Spirit never drives but only leads, am I willingly co-operating with that leading?
ch15.sub: Melchizedeks, Vorondadeks, Lanonandeks, and Life Carriers
ch15.sum: As the Paradise Sons proceed from the Deities of Paradise, so in the local universe there are orders of sons born of the Creator Son and the Universe Mother Spirit together. The Melchizedeks are the teaching elder brothers and the first to act in every emergency; the Vorondadeks, as Constellation Fathers, uphold the larger framework of local universe government; and the Lanonandeks rule the systems and planets. The Life Carriers plant life on new worlds and foster it until will appears. This chapter surveys the nature and service of these sons and shows how divine rule does not remain on high but steps down level by level until it comes near the evolving creature. Such nearness carries a risk of going astray, yet accepting that risk was part of a loving design.
ch15.s1: The Orders of Local Universe Sonship
ch15.s1.u1.k: Dual Deity in the local universe, the Son and the Spirit, brings forth three high orders of sons and the Life Carriers.
ch15.s1.u1.p: As triune Deity on Paradise brings forth three orders of sons, so in the local universe the Creator Son and the Mother Spirit together bring forth sons who correspond to them. The pattern established above is repeated below. Because these sons are born in the local universe and work for it, they know and serve the affairs of our universe from closer at hand than anyone else.
ch15.s1.u2.k: The Melchizedeks are the first order of sons able to serve the evolutionary races without incarnation.
ch15.s1.u2.p: In the great descent of personality the Melchizedeks stand about midway between the highest Divinity and the lowest creature of will. That is why they can serve the evolutionary races directly without incarnation. A higher being who would serve a lower one must first understand it, and that understanding springs from their place midway between above and below.
ch15.s1.u3.k: The Melchizedeks serve as the eldest son of a large family, taking responsibility on themselves.
ch15.s1.u3.p: An eldest son does not merely do what he is told. Much of the Melchizedeks' work is voluntary and self-imposed. They patrol the universe on their own initiative and, as unprejudiced observers, win the confidence of all intelligent beings. Responsibility shouldered freely earns deeper trust than responsibility merely assigned.
ch15.s2: The Melchizedeks: Teachers and Emergency Ministers
ch15.s2.u1.k: The world Melchizedek is where the local universe education of ascending mortals begins.
ch15.s2.u1.p: The Melchizedeks are above all teachers. Every ascender who completes constellation training lands on their world and enters the Salvington educational system. The remark that one never forgets that first day, even after reaching Paradise, reminds us that learning is at the heart of the ascending career. Salvation is both a moment and the beginning of an endless education.
ch15.s2.u2.k: The Melchizedeks are the first to act in emergencies on all worlds where will creatures dwell.
ch15.s2.u2.p: When a planetary government collapses or a plan is threatened with failure, the Melchizedeks are the first to go. They may serve as temporary custodians, and on rare occasions have even appeared in the likeness of mortal flesh. Machiventa, who came to Urantia as the sage of Salem, is one instance of such emergency ministry. In times of crisis help has already been provided.
ch15.s2.u3.k: The Melchizedeks are well-nigh perfect in wisdom but not infallible in judgment.
ch15.s2.u3.p: This revelation does not conceal the mistakes even of high beings. Melchizedeks, well-nigh perfect in wisdom, have sometimes erred in minor matters when alone on planetary missions, choosing to do things their supervisors did not afterward approve. Near-perfect wisdom is not the same as infallible judgment. In a universe moving toward perfection, mistakes are not to be hidden but become occasions for learning.
ch15.s3: Vorondadeks and Lanonandeks: The Ruling Sons
ch15.s3.u1.k: The Vorondadeks rule as Constellation Fathers and watch as observers over isolated worlds.
ch15.s3.u1.p: The Vorondadeks are the sons who stand at the head of the constellation governments. Yet their service does not end with ruling. On worlds isolated through rebellion a Vorondadek observer remains until normal status is restored. A planet segregated in darkness, as Urantia has been, is never abandoned; it lies under the watchful eye of those on high.
ch15.s3.u2.k: The Constellation Fathers form the Creator Son's supreme advisory cabinet and are intrusted with sovereign powers in crises.
ch15.s3.u2.p: The Creator Son does not decide alone. One hundred Constellation Fathers serve as his advisory cabinet and deliberate with him on the welfare of the constellations and the unity of universe administration. In critical situations the Vorondadeks are intrusted with the full delegation of sovereign power. Delegation and counsel are marks of wisdom in universe government.
ch15.s3.u3.k: The Lanonandeks draw nearer the creatures and so serve the more, but they also run a greater risk of going astray.
ch15.s3.u3.p: Most system sovereigns and Planetary Princes are Lanonandeks. Because they stand somewhat lower in divinity, they can draw nearer the intelligent races and render great service in the subordinate units of the universe. But nearness brings risk. That the possibility of departure grows as the place of service descends is borne out by the history of Satania.
ch15.s3.u4.k: The default of Lanonandeks is no fault in creatorship, and a way of salvation is open to them too.
ch15.s3.u4.p: They could have been made divinely perfect from the start, but they were deliberately not so made, that they might better understand and draw near to evolutionary creatures. It was a risk accepted for the sake of understanding. And for those who went astray a merciful way of rehabilitation has been provided, though they may never return to the posts they betrayed. Mercy and justice work together.
ch15.s4: The Life Carriers: Sons Who Plant Life
ch15.s4.u1.k: Life does not originate spontaneously; it is given through the Life Carriers with the spark of the Mother Spirit.
ch15.s4.u1.p: The Life Carriers design life, carry it to the planets, and plant it there. Yet the mystery of life itself does not come from them. They formulate the life plasm, but the spark that enlivens the body and presages the mind is supplied by the Universe Mother Spirit. Life begins where skilled design meets the divine breath.
ch15.s4.u2.k: When a being with will appears the Life Carriers' work is ended, and they do not interfere with will.
ch15.s4.u2.p: Even those who planted life withdraw their hands before moral choice. At the moment will appears their work is finished, and they manipulate the evolving life no further. That the Life Carriers may neither experiment with nor dominate will shows the universe's deep respect for personal freedom. A choosing being is not an object to be manipulated.
ch15.qs1: What might the attitude of an eldest son, shouldering responsibility unasked as the Melchizedeks do, look like in my community?
ch15.qs2: How does knowing that even high beings err and are corrected affect the way I treat my own mistakes and those of others?
ch15.qs3: If even the Life Carriers do not interfere with will, how fully do I respect the choices of other people?
ch16.sub: The Ministering Spirits of Time and the Guardians of Destiny
ch16.sum: Angels are not winged figures of legend but real ministering spirits born of the Infinite Spirit and his daughters. From the supernaphim of the central universe to the seraphim and cherubim of the local universe, they serve the ascending will creatures throughout creation. The seraphim of the local universe are children of the Universe Mother Spirit, created a little above man; they share most human emotions and form one link in the chain that bridges the gap between matter and spirit. This chapter considers the nature of angels, the origin and organization of the seraphim, the ministry of the guardians of destiny, and the companionship of man and angel that continues beyond death. Angels are not objects of worship but fellow servants with us of God.
ch16.s1.u1.k: Angels are ministering-spirit associates of ascending will creatures, each a distinct personality.
ch16.s1.u1.p: Angels are not forces that carry out God's commands like machines; they are highly individualized personalities. They rest, enjoy change, and delight in association; they are social beings. Below them they serve evolving mortals, and above them they work with divine personalities. The angelic world is a community of fellow workers before it is a hierarchy.
ch16.s1.u2.k: Angels are bodiless spirit beings, yet they know human beings as they are and love them.
ch16.s1.u2.p: Man cannot see the angels, but the angels see man as he is. They understand the mode of mortal life and share man's emotions and sentiments. This passage portrays angels not as remote and cold beings but as friends who sympathize from close at hand. The effort to understand and love them bears good fruit.
ch16.s1.u3.k: Love angels but do not adore them; angels are neither man's judges nor his accusers.
ch16.s1.u3.p: Too much interest in angels easily slides into veneration, and the text firmly closes that road. Angels are fellow servants who worship God together with man. Nor do they condemn man because their spiritual status is higher. If those mightier than we bring no accusation, we have no reason to prejudge our fellows.
ch16.s2: Seraphim: Children of the Mother Spirit
ch16.s2.u1.k: The seraphim are the offspring of the Universe Mother Spirit's first solitary act of spirit reproduction.
ch16.s2.u1.p: After the Creator Son and the Mother Spirit have together created many sons, the Son creates the Material Sons while the Mother Spirit, for the first time acting alone, brings forth the seraphim. Angels are thus in a special sense the Mother Spirit's children. Since human mind also springs from that same Mother Spirit, angels and men are close, like children of one mother.
ch16.s2.u2.k: Seraphim are not male and female but negative and positive, and they work in pairs.
ch16.s2.u2.p: Most angelic assignments require two angels. The pairing springs from function rather than sex emotion, yet the angels are exceedingly personal and affectionate. The principle of a pair working as one is the basic unit of service in the angelic world as in the human world. Some tasks cannot be done alone.
ch16.s2.u3.k: The gap between the material and spiritual worlds is bridged by a series of beings from man to seraphim.
ch16.s2.u3.p: There is no unbridgeable gap in the universe. Between man and the seraphim stand the midwayers and the cherubim, filling the borderlands of matter, morontia, and spirit. This chain is a bridge laid so that the ascender is never left alone at any stage. And within one person's experience the Thought Adjuster weaves these many levels into one.
ch16.s3.u1.k: Guardian angels are no myth; a personal angel is assigned to the mortal who reaches the third circle.
ch16.s3.u1.p: When Jesus spoke of the angels of little children, he was not speaking in parable. Angelic care deepens in step with a person's spiritual growth. At first one angel watches over many people together, but when a mind breaks through the inertia of animal legacy and reaches the third circle, a pair of angels is devoted to that one person alone. Growth invites closer companionship.
ch16.s3.u2.k: Angels hold a deep affection for men and find it hard to understand why men let fear rule them.
ch16.s3.u2.p: Angels share most human emotions, but fear is hard for them to comprehend. That even a person of faith should be gripped by dread and anxiety seems strange to them. The observation awakens rather than rebukes us. For a being held in God's care, fear is a guest that does not really belong.
ch16.s3.u3.k: Seraphim stimulate the mind from without inward, leading not to ease but to growth.
ch16.s3.u3.p: If the Adjuster works from within through the soul, the seraphim work from without through the social, ethical, and moral environment. To be led by an angel does not mean that difficulties disappear; it means being brought before the rugged hills of moral choice. Angels are beside us less to shelter us than to help us grow.
ch16.s3.u4.k: Angels never invade the sanctity of the human mind or interfere with the free action of the will.
ch16.s3.u4.p: Angels stay close beside us and care for us sincerely, yet they leave the choice to man to the very end. They influence only in ways consistent with the dignity of personality and never manipulate the will. The figure of angels who "weep" at our stubbornness shows how painful a love that will not coerce can be.
ch16.s4.u1.k: The guardian seraphim keeps the survival values of the sleeping soul and helps reassemble the personality on the mansion world.
ch16.s4.u1.p: At death the Adjuster departs, but the survival values of the soul are entrusted to the guardian angel. When the two meet again on the mansion world, the personality awakens in a new morontia form. Then for the first time a person sees the angels who were beside him all his life. Resurrection is not an event met alone but a reunion with long-time companions.
ch16.s4.u2.k: Guiding one soul to the portals of Paradise is the way the seraphim open their own high destiny.
ch16.s4.u2.p: Angelic service is not one-sided sacrifice. While guarding a mortal on the path of divine destiny, the seraphim are also determining their own destiny. That is why guardian of destiny is the most highly prized angelic assignment. In this arrangement the one who serves and the one served reach Paradise together, revealing the mutuality of love in the universe.
ch16.qs1: How does the fact that angels bring no accusation against man lead me to reconsider my habit of judging others?
ch16.qs2: What are the fears and anxieties that angels find so hard to understand in me, and how can I meet them with faith?
ch16.qs3: Am I willing to accept a leading that takes me not toward ease but toward growth?
ch17.sub: The Living Intelligences Who Regulate the Physical Universe
ch17.sum: The physical universe is not a machine that runs by itself. The Seven Supreme Power Directors, created collectively by the Seven Master Spirits, the vast host of power centers derived from them, and the Master Physical Controllers beneath them transform the force flowing from Paradise into energy and matter and regulate its circuits. Some of them are persons of high will and intelligence; others are living mechanisms possessed of intelligence but without power of choice. This chapter considers why the power directors are so hard to understand, what kind of beings they are and how they work, and how energy itself reflects a divine order. The foundation of the universe is material, yet even matter is in the keeping of living intelligence and at last returns to Paradise.
ch17.s1.u1.k: The power directors and their associates have been the least understood universe personalities on Urantia.
ch17.s1.u1.p: Mankind has long known of angels but has heard almost nothing of the beings who govern the physical world. Religion has mostly attended to spiritual beings on high, while science has explained nature solely as impersonal law. This revelation places living intelligences in the gap between them. Behind the order of stars and atoms there is also a guiding hand.
ch17.s1.u2.k: Mortals find it hard to envisage the power directors, yet in the ascending career they will work with some of them.
ch17.s1.u2.p: A material creature can at least imagine spiritual beings by contrast, but a semimaterial being that is neither spirit nor matter is hard even to picture. Yet these beings are not unrelated to man. On reaching the mansion worlds the ascender works freely with the Morontia Power Supervisors. Even unfamiliar colleagues belong in the end to the same universe family.
ch17.s1.u3.k: Matter-energy consists in the Universal Father, and the power directors transmute energy into matter.
ch17.s1.u3.p: To understand the power directors we must first recognize that matter is not a realm apart from God. Matter seems to possess powers of its own, but the gravity lines of its energies come from Paradise and depend upon it. The creation of energy and the bestowal of life are the prerogatives of the Father and his associate Creators, and the power directors receive that stream and transmute energy into matter. The work of those who tend the physical world is the tending of the Father's universe.
ch17.s2: Supreme Power Directors and Power Centers
ch17.s2.u1.k: The Seven Supreme Power Directors are the first semimaterial progeny of spirit ancestry and the ancestors of the whole power system.
ch17.s2.u1.p: When the Seven Master Spirits create individually, spiritual angelic orders come forth; when they create together, these semimaterial beings appear. This lineage from spirit to the quasi-physical shows that spirit and matter are not two worlds sealed off from each other. And the fundamental uniformity of physical administration testifies that the universe stands under a single order.
ch17.s2.u2.k: The power centers are persons of high will and exquisite intelligence, the intellect of the universe power system.
ch17.s2.u2.p: The steadiness of physical law is often taken as a sign that intelligence is absent. But according to this revelation, at the directing centers of the universe power circuits are volitional beings with Third Source personality. The regularity of law appears not because intelligence is missing but because a perfect intelligence works faithfully. Order is the trace of mind.
ch17.s2.u3.k: Power centers and physical controllers are created perfect, do not evolve, and never for an instant leave their duty.
ch17.s2.u3.p: Unlike ascending mortals they have neither training nor promotion. They serve forever in the post first assigned, and having no ascendant past to recall, they never play. The universal plan makes no provision for any interruption of the lines of energy. While men rest and sleep, the faithfulness of those who uphold the world never pauses.
ch17.s2.u4.k: The power directors do not originate energy but modify and directionize it, and relate to gravity only by resisting it.
ch17.s2.u4.p: The source of energy is Paradise; the power directors handle it but do not create it. Their role is clearly bounded. The revelator also confesses that he cannot explain how they work. This humble admission that they are living and personal yet beyond our comprehension teaches an attitude that does not presume to settle the mysteries of the universe.
ch17.s3.u1.k: Personality is not necessarily a concomitant of mind; controllers without choice are still highly intelligent.
ch17.s3.u1.p: This passage contains an important theological principle that distinguishes mind from personality. Mind can think without being able to choose. Some physical controllers look like machines, yet they disclose the differential function of intelligence. Personality, by contrast, is the Father's gift and carries will and decision. The contrast shows how precious man's freedom of choice is.
ch17.s3.u2.k: The physical controllers are not responsible for all energy misbehavior on Urantia.
ch17.s3.u2.p: People often blame God or celestial beings for natural disasters. But Urantia is a small planet lying in the lines of tremendous energies, and not every energy disturbance is the controllers' responsibility. The controllers mobilize great numbers in an effort to equalize these energies. Discernment is needed not to read every event as a direct expression of the divine will.
ch17.s3.u3.k: The physical controllers maintain the balance of energy and matter, and the universe at last settles into stable circuits.
ch17.s3.u3.p: Even vast events such as the collision and dissolution of stars are not victories of disorder but part of a process moving toward equilibrium. The physical controllers watch over the balance of energy and matter, and at last the larger systems are stabilized and swung into the balanced circuits of the superuniverses. After that, no more collisions or devastating catastrophes occur in them. The turmoil of the cosmos moves toward settledness.
ch17.s4.u1.k: The organizing of energy in the presence of power directors is named one of the "infinities of divinity."
ch17.s4.u1.p: The power directors are catalyzers who segment and organize energy merely by their presence. This implies that something inherent in energy responds to them. The Melchizedeks named this mystery one of the "infinities of divinity." Even in the depths of the material world there is a trace of divinity, and before it inquiry turns into reverence.
ch17.s4.u2.k: Energy proceeds from Paradise after the divine order, and at last returns to Paradise.
ch17.s4.u2.p: Energy is fashioned after the likeness of the three Gods embraced in one and is a manifestation of the uncaused Cause, the Universal Father. Eternal but not infinite, it returns to Paradise along its ordained circuit, however many ages that may require. Every force the power directors handle moves within a vast current of homecoming toward the Father.
ch17.qs1: How does my view of the world change when I see the regularity of nature as the faithful care of living intelligences?
ch17.qs2: Compared with beings who have mind but cannot choose, what responsibility does my own freedom of choice require of me?
ch17.qs3: How do I exercise discernment about the impulse to interpret every natural disaster or accident as the will of God?
ch18.sub: Universe Dwellers Who Neither Ascend nor Descend
ch18.sum: The universe is not made up only of ascenders who stay for a while and move on, and of Sons who descend from above to minister. There are also permanent citizens who remain where they were born and carry on the life and culture of their worlds: the Susatia of Salvington, the univitatia of Edentia, the Material Sons and Daughters of the system capitals, and the midway creatures of the planets. By and large they neither ascend nor descend, yet they offer their growing experience to the universe on their own level. Ascending mortals meet and learn from them at each stage of the journey, and in the homes of the Material Sons they gain the experience of parenthood. This chapter considers who these citizens are and why their abiding is indispensable to the universe. Because there are those who move on, the faithfulness of those who remain shines all the more.
ch18.s1.u1.k: The natives of the local universe form a relatively permanent citizenship, offering their experience on their level of origin.
ch18.s1.u1.p: Between the great currents of ascent and descent there is another way of life: abiding. The permanent citizens also grow through experience, but instead of leaving for higher places their growth enriches the place where they stand. The Susatia of Salvington are the first example. Because some remain, those who come and go always find a familiar home.
ch18.s1.u2.k: The univitatia are the permanent citizens of Edentia, and morontia mortals are attuned in form to their scale.
ch18.s1.u2.p: The univitatia are the natives of Edentia's seventy major spheres, and their visible form differs on each. Each time the ascender moves from one sphere to the next, his morontia form is attuned to their ascending scale. Ascension is not merely a change of place but a process of learning to fit oneself to the life of those who dwell there.
ch18.s1.u3.k: The univitatia, seventy orders of varied intellect, teach practical socialization and build the artistic culture of the constellation.
ch18.s1.u3.p: Alike in spirit yet as varied in intellect as mortals are, the univitatia make good teachers for ascenders. They teach occupational and practical socialization, and with the artisans they make the constellation worlds a beautiful stage of transition culture. From them the ascender learns how differing intellects can live together in one spirit.
ch18.s2: The Material Sons and Daughters of the System Capital
ch18.s2.u1.k: The Material Sons and Daughters are a reproducing order of sonship created by the Creator Son in dual form, permanent citizens of the system capital.
ch18.s2.u1.p: The Material Sons and Daughters are a reproducing order of sonship, created male and female. Their progeny become relatively permanent citizens of a system capital, while some are commissioned as Planetary Adams and go forth to the evolutionary worlds. Unlike the higher spirit Sons, they form families and bear children. Sex and family have had their place in the universe order from the beginning.
ch18.s2.u2.k: The Material Sons are the last physical link in the chain of personalities from divinity to humanity, and on Jerusem they experiment with self-government.
ch18.s2.u2.p: The Material Sons are a visible and contactable intermediary between the unseen Planetary Prince and the mortal races. In them the chain of personalities descending from above at last touches matter. On Jerusem they also govern themselves by universal suffrage and representative government, moving toward fuller autonomy. The maturing of social order is itself part of the divine plan.
ch18.s2.u3.k: The experience of parenthood is indispensable training for every ascender who would attain the Father.
ch18.s2.u3.p: To know God as Father one must know a parent's heart. Thus no mortal, midwayer, or seraphim may enter the Corps of the Finality without parenthood or an equivalent experience. Those who missed this experience on earth learn it in the homes of the Material Sons on Jerusem. The homes of permanent citizens become schools for ascenders.
ch18.s3.u1.k: The midwayers are permanent inhabitants who remain on the planet, linking the changing seraphic administrations.
ch18.s3.u1.p: The first permanent citizens met on the ascending journey are the midwayers of our own planet. The seraphim come and go with their assignments, but the midwayers remain. They are at once natives of the planet and ministers, preserving continuity amid changing administrations. The memory and responsibility of a world are entrusted to those who stay there.
ch18.s3.u2.k: As citizens of Urantia the midwayers work persistently for its progress and keep growing in wisdom and experience.
ch18.s3.u2.p: The midwayers have a kinship interest in the destiny of this planet. Though brought into existence fully developed, they never cease to grow in wisdom and experience, and they possess a genuine evolutionary culture. That unseen cousins living on the same world are working with us for the progress of our civilization reminds us that mankind is not alone.
ch18.s3.u3.k: The generations of men forget, but the midwayers remember, and their memory is the treasure house of planetary tradition.
ch18.s3.u3.p: Human generations forget, but the midwayers, the immortal citizens of this planet, remember. Through their memory the culture of a planet remains ever present. That the life and teachings of Jesus have been restored to us through the midwayers shows well the worth of the memory of those who remain.
ch18.s4: The Survival Plan and the Humblest Citizens
ch18.s4.u1.k: The whole universe organization is devoted to the survival plan of bringing God down to man and carrying man up to God.
ch18.s4.u1.p: High spirits, angels, and midwayers stand in different places but serve the same purpose: to bring God down to man and, in partnership, to carry man up to God. And this plan is open not only to mortals but to midwayers as well. Even the abiding citizens at last share in the great current of ascent.
ch18.s4.u2.k: The spornagia are unique creatures without personality whose identity persists, and they may someday reach a higher destiny.
ch18.s4.u2.p: The spornagia who tend the architectural worlds of the system capital do not respond to the adjutants of worship and wisdom and so have no surviving soul. Yet the experiential identity formed by their five-adjutant mind persists. And there is hope that someday they may rise from the animal level to spiritual achievement. The care of the universe is not closed even to its humblest creatures.
ch18.qs1: Between moving on and remaining, how is faithfully keeping my present place connected with my own growth?
ch18.qs2: If the experience of parenthood is essential to knowing God as Father, what am I learning through caring for someone else?
ch18.qs3: What part can I take in preserving the memory and traditions of my community?
